theorem Rat.AdeleRing.zero_discrete : ∃ U : Set (AdeleRing (𝓞 ℚ) ℚ),
    IsOpen U ∧ (algebraMap ℚ (AdeleRing (𝓞 ℚ) ℚ)) ⁻¹' U = {0} := by
  use {f | ∀ v, f v ∈ (Metric.ball 0 1)} ×ˢ
    {f | ∀ v , f v ∈ IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.adicCompletionIntegers ℚ v}
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · dsimp
    sorry -- issue #252 -- should be easy (product of opens is open, product of integers is surely
          -- known to be open)
  · apply subset_antisymm
    · intro x hx
      rw [Set.mem_preimage] at hx
      simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff]
      have : (algebraMap ℚ (AdeleRing (𝓞 ℚ) ℚ)) x =
        (algebraMap ℚ (InfiniteAdeleRing ℚ) x, algebraMap ℚ (FiniteAdeleRing (𝓞 ℚ) ℚ) x)
      · rfl
      rw [this] at hx
      clear this
      rw [Set.mem_prod] at hx
      obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hx
      dsimp only at h1 h2
      simp only [Metric.mem_ball, dist_zero_right, Set.mem_setOf_eq,
        InfiniteAdeleRing.algebraMap_apply, UniformSpace.Completion.norm_coe] at h1
      simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at h2
      specialize h1 Rat.infinitePlace
      change ‖(x : ℂ)‖ < 1 at h1
      simp at h1
      have intx: ∃ (y:ℤ), y = x
      · obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.mem_integers_of_valuation_le_one
            ℚ x <| fun v ↦ by
          specialize h2 v
          letI : UniformSpace ℚ := v.adicValued.toUniformSpace
          rw [IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.mem_adicCompletionIntegers] at h2
          rwa [← IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuedAdicCompletion_eq_valuation']
        use Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv z
        rw [← hz]
        apply Rat.ringOfIntegersEquiv_eq_algebraMap
      obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := intx
      simp only [abs_lt] at h1
      norm_cast at h1 ⊢
      -- We need the next line because `norm_cast` is for some reason producing a `negSucc 0`.
      -- I haven't been able to isolate this behaviour even in a standalone lemma.
      -- We could also make `omega` more robust against accidental appearances of `negSucc`.
      rw [Int.negSucc_eq] at h1
      omega
    · intro x
      simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff, Set.mem_preimage]
      rintro rfl
      simp only [map_zero]
      change (0, 0) ∈ _
      simp only [Prod.mk_zero_zero, Set.mem_prod, Prod.fst_zero, Prod.snd_zero]
      constructor
      · simp only [Metric.mem_ball, dist_zero_right, Set.mem_setOf_eq]
        intro v
        have : ‖(0:InfiniteAdeleRing ℚ) v‖ = 0

          rfl
        simp [this, zero_lt_one]
      · simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]
        intro v
        apply zero_mem

   - The field \( K \) is embedded diagonally into \( A_K \), meaning each element \( x \in K \) is mapped to the tuple \( (x)' \) where each component corresponds to the completion of \( x \) at each place.

   - The quotient space \( A_K / \text{im}(K) \) consists of cosets of the form \( a + \text{im}(K) \) where \( a \in A_K \).

   - The adele ring \( A_K \) is a locally compact topological ring.
   - The image \( \text{im}(K) \) under the diagonal embedding is a discrete subgroup of \( A_K \).

rag.content:
/-- First version, with pointwise equicontinuity and range in a compact space. -/
theorem arzela_ascoli₁ [CompactSpace β] (A : Set (α →ᵇ β)) (closed : IsClosed A)
    (H : Equicontinuous ((↑) : A → α → β)) : IsCompact A := by
  simp_rw [Equicontinuous, Metric.equicontinuousAt_iff_pair] at H
  refine isCompact_of_totallyBounded_isClosed ?_ closed
  refine totallyBounded_of_finite_discretization fun ε ε0 => ?_
  rcases exists_between ε0 with ⟨ε₁, ε₁0, εε₁⟩
  let ε₂ := ε₁ / 2 / 2
  /- We have to find a finite discretization of `u`, i.e., finite information
    that is sufficient to reconstruct `u` up to `ε`. This information will be
    provided by the values of `u` on a sufficiently dense set `tα`,
    slightly translated to fit in a finite `ε₂`-dense set `tβ` in the image. Such
    sets exist by compactness of the source and range. Then, to check that these
    data determine the function up to `ε`, one uses the control on the modulus of
    continuity to extend the closeness on tα to closeness everywhere. -/
  have ε₂0 : ε₂ > 0 := half_pos (half_pos ε₁0)
  have : ∀ x : α, ∃ U, x ∈ U ∧ IsOpen U ∧
      ∀ y ∈ U, ∀ z ∈ U, ∀ {f : α →ᵇ β}, f ∈ A → dist (f y) (f z) < ε₂ := fun x =>
    let ⟨U, nhdsU, hU⟩ := H x _ ε₂0
    let ⟨V, VU, openV, xV⟩ := _root_.mem_nhds_iff.1 nhdsU
    ⟨V, xV, openV, fun y hy z hz f hf => hU y (VU hy) z (VU hz) ⟨f, hf⟩⟩
  choose U hU using this
  /- For all `x`, the set `hU x` is an open set containing `x` on which the elements of `A`
    fluctuate by at most `ε₂`.
    We extract finitely many of these sets that cover the whole space, by compactness. -/
  obtain ⟨tα : Set α, _, hfin, htα : univ ⊆ ⋃ x ∈ tα, U x⟩ :=
    isCompact_univ.elim_finite_subcover_image (fun x _ => (hU x).2.1) fun x _ =>
      mem_biUnion (mem_univ _) (hU x).1
  rcases hfin.nonempty_fintype with ⟨_⟩
  obtain ⟨tβ : Set β, _, hfin, htβ : univ ⊆ ⋃y ∈ tβ, ball y ε₂⟩ :=
    @finite_cover_balls_of_compact β _ _ isCompact_univ _ ε₂0
  rcases hfin.nonempty_fintype with ⟨_⟩
  -- Associate to every point `y` in the space a nearby point `F y` in `tβ`
  choose F hF using fun y => show ∃ z ∈ tβ, dist y z < ε₂ by simpa using htβ (mem_univ y)
  -- `F : β → β`, `hF : ∀ (y : β), F y ∈ tβ ∧ dist y (F y) < ε₂`
  /- Associate to every function a discrete approximation, mapping each point in `tα`
    to a point in `tβ` close to its true image by the function. -/
  classical
  refine ⟨tα → tβ, by infer_instance, fun f a => ⟨F (f.1 a), (hF (f.1 a)).1⟩, ?_⟩
  rintro ⟨f, hf⟩ ⟨g, hg⟩ f_eq_g
  -- If two functions have the same approximation, then they are within distance `ε`
  refine lt_of_le_of_lt ((dist_le <| le_of_lt ε₁0).2 fun x => ?_) εε₁
  obtain ⟨x', x'tα, hx'⟩ := mem_iUnion₂.1 (htα (mem_univ x))
  calc
    dist (f x) (g x) ≤ dist (f x) (f x') + dist (g x) (g x') + dist (f x') (g x') :=
      dist_triangle4_right _ _ _ _
    _ ≤ ε₂ + ε₂ + ε₁ / 2 := by
      refine le_of_lt (add_lt_add (add_lt_add ?_ ?_) ?_)
      · exact (hU x').2.2 _ hx' _ (hU x').1 hf
      · exact (hU x').2.2 _ hx' _ (hU x').1 hg
      · have F_f_g : F (f x') = F (g x') :=
          (congr_arg (fun f : tα → tβ => (f ⟨x', x'tα⟩ : β)) f_eq_g :)
        calc
          dist (f x') (g x') ≤ dist (f x') (F (f x')) + dist (g x') (F (f x')) :=
            dist_triangle_right _ _ _
          _ = dist (f x') (F (f x')) + dist (g x') (F (g x')) := by rw [F_f_g]
          _ < ε₂ + ε₂ := (add_lt_add (hF (f x')).2 (hF (g x')).2)
          _ = ε₁ / 2 := add_halves _
    _ = ε₁ := by rw [add_halves, add_halves]

To understand why the quotient space \( \A_{\mathbb{Q}} / \mathbb{Q} \) is compact, we need to delve into the properties of adele rings and quotient spaces in topology.

The adele ring \( \A_{\mathbb{Q}} \) is a locally compact topological ring that can be constructed as a restricted product of completions of the rational numbers \( \mathbb{Q} \). These completions include both the real numbers \( \mathbb{R} \) and the \( p \)-adic numbers \( \mathbb{Q}_p \) for each prime \( p \). Each of these completions is a locally compact space.

When we consider the additive map from \( \mathbb{Q} \) to \( \A_{\mathbb{Q}} \), we are lifting rational numbers into this adele ring. The image of \( \mathbb{Q} \) under this map is a discrete subgroup of \( \A_{\mathbb{Q}} \), meaning that it sits "isolated" within the larger space of adeles. This is because each \( \mathbb{Q}_p \) is totally disconnected, and the rational numbers themselves inherit this property in a certain sense.

By taking the quotient \( \A_{\mathbb{Q}} / \mathbb{Q} \), we are essentially collapsing this discrete subgroup to a point, resulting in a space that "avoids" these discrete points. The local compactness of \( \A_{\mathbb{Q}} \) and the discreteness of \( \mathbb{Q} \) within it are key factors in ensuring that the quotient space \( \A_{\mathbb{Q}} / \mathbb{Q} \) is compact.

Compactness, in this context, means that every open cover of the quotient space has a finite subcover. This property is closely tied to the notion of being "closed and bounded" in Euclidean spaces, though the exact analogy is not direct here. Still, it reflects the idea that the quotient space is manageable and does not "gesture towards infinity" in a way that would prevent compactness.

In summary, the compactness of \( \A_{\mathbb{Q}} / \mathbb{Q} \) arises from the interplay between the local compactness of the adele ring and the discrete nature of the rationals within it, ensuring that this quotient space is, in a sense, finite and well-behaved topologically.

informal_proof:
To demonstrate that the set \( \{q\} \) is open in the adele ring \( \mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}} \), we employ the concept of homeomorphisms in topology. A fundamental property of topological spaces is that a subset is open if it can be mapped to an open set in another space via a homeomorphism.

1. **Starting Point**: Begin with the basic open set around zero in the adele ring, provided by the `zero_discrete` lemma. This gives us an open neighborhood \( V \) around the zero element in \( \mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}} \).

2. **Algebra Map and Homeomorphism**: Consider the algebra map \( \iota: \mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}} \) and apply it to the rational number \( q \), obtaining \( \iota(q) = q_{\mathbb{A}} \) in the adele ring. Define a function \( f \) as the difference \( f = \text{Homeomorph.subLeft}(q_{\mathbb{A}}) \), which acts as a homeomorphism on \( \mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}} \).

3. **Preimage of Open Set**: Since \( f \) is a homeomorphism, it maps open sets to open sets. Taking the preimage \( f^{-1}(V) \) of the open set \( V \) around zero under this homeomorphism \( f \), we obtain an open set around \( q_{\mathbb{A}} \).

4. **Singleton Open Set**: By construction, the preimage \( f^{-1}(V) \) contains only the point \( q \) in the adele ring, as this is the image of zero under the homeomorphism \( f \). Therefore, \( \{q\} \) is an open set in \( \mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}} \).

5. **Verification**: To confirm, we verify that the composition of maps preserves the open property and aligns the neighborhoods accordingly, ensuring that \( \{q\} \) is indeed open in the topology of \( \mathbb{A}_{\mathbb{Q}} \).

This step-by-step approach leverages the properties of homeomorphisms and open sets to establish that each singleton set containing a rational number is open in the adele ring, thereby proving the statement.

informal_proof:
To show the existence of such an open neighborhood \( U \) in the Adele ring \( \mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q} \), we utilize its construction as a restricted product of local fields. Specifically, the Adele ring is formed by taking the product of the real numbers and all p-adic number fields, but only considering tuples where the components are in increasingly small neighborhoods around zero as we move to finite places. This ensures that \( U \) is an open set in \( \mathbb{A}_\mathbb{Q} \).

Next, we define \( U \) as the product of open balls in each local field centered at zero with radius 1. That is, in the real numbers, this corresponds to the interval \( (-1, 1) \), and in each p-adic field, it corresponds to the p-adic integers. The intersection of all these open sets within the restricted product defines our neighborhood \( U \).

To prove that the preimage of \( U \) under the algebra map is simply the zero element, we proceed by contradiction. Assume there exists a non-zero rational number \( q \) whose image under the algebra map is contained within \( U \). This would imply that \( q \) lies within every open ball of radius 1 in both the real and p-adic places. However, this is impossible because in the real numbers, \( q \) cannot be within \( (-1, 1) \) if \( q \) is non-zero and finite. Consequently, no non-zero element of \( \mathbb{Q} \) can map into \( U \), confirming that the preimage of \( U \) under the algebra map is indeed just the single element \( 0 \).

Thus, the existence of such an open neighborhood \( U \) with the desired properties is established, completing the proof.
